q: we present a systematic empirical study of harness effects in SE agents.
r: Include: controlled comparison of harnesses and models on the same SE benchmarks, with component-level ablation (evaluation method, EC6 ii).

q: We introduce WIDESWE to evaluate coding agents on such cross-repository tasks.
r: Include: new benchmark of 60 feature and 60 bug-fix cross-repository tasks, seven agent configurations compared.

q: We applied it in an observational study of ten experienced developers who used GitHub Copilot on an unfamiliar codebase.
r: Include: main contribution is an evaluation workflow and instruments for human-agent interaction and understanding (human-effort measurement), EC6 ii.

q: We introduced OpenGameEval, a play-time-verified benchmark for agentic software development inside a deployed game engine.
r: Include: new benchmark with 16 attempts per task and exploration metrics (evaluation method, EC6 ii) despite the single game-engine domain.

q: coordination among parallel coding agents is a scheduling problem.
r: Include: new benchmark (NP-Bench) with three-arm design comparing coordination of parallel coding agents on integration outcomes.

q: We introduce AgentSWE, a benchmark for agent software engineering spanning three stages of the agent development lifecycle
r: Include: new benchmark where coding agents build agents from natural-language requirements (project level), several models and harnesses compared.

q: We introduce SWE-Maintain, 100 three-event maintenance episodes reconstructed from 50 real-world Python repositories
r: Include: paired evaluation design is the main contribution (EC6 ii), tasks extend or modify code over episodes, not pure issue repair.
EC6: cost analysis of published SWE-bench trajectories (issue repair), not a code-development evaluation.

q: We presented ANCHOR, a benchmark that reframes evaluation in agentic coding from task completion alone to task completion under explicit engineering constraints.
r: Include: new benchmark and trajectory-grounded evaluation of constraint following on repository tasks across 19 agent configurations (EC6 ii).

q: We identify Starting-State Robustness, the ability to maintain performance on a task when the starting state already contains earlier work on that task
r: Include: new evaluation dimension and benchmark comparing five agents from clean and residual starts (EC6 ii).
